gaps.sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

gaps.sentence: He ___ all knowledge of the missing file.
gaps.explanation: 'Deny all knowledge of something' is the fixed phrase.
